paragraphs.text: Sound notifications for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): play a sound when a task completes, fails, or waits
for approval — with per-category switches.
# dsh-sound-notify
**English** | 简体中文
Sound notifications for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. When a DSH task finishes, fails, or stops to wai
t for you, this plugin plays a short sound on the machine running DSH — and gives you a switch for e
is plugin plays a short sound on the machine running DSH — and gives you a switch for each category.
## Why
DSH sessions are long-running. Without a sound, you keep alt-tabbing back to the window to check whe
ther the agent is done. This plugin makes "it stopped" audible:
| Event | Trigger | Sound |

| Task completed | turn ends with `completed` | `sounds/success.aac` |
| Task failed | turn ends wit
h `error` / `max-tokens`, or an API request failed and a retry was scheduled (`llm/retry`) | `sounds

/fail.aac` |
| Waiting for you | approval prompt (`approval/asked`), `ask_user_question`, turn abort
ed / blocked / interrupted | `sounds/stop.aac` |
Playback happens in the **DSH host process** with the OS audio player (macOS `afplay`, Linux `paplay
`), so it works even when the browser tab is backgrounded, minimized, or closed. The sound plays on
the machine that runs DSH.
## Features
- **Three independent switches**, all enabled by default, stored in DSH settings and applied live —

no restart needed.
- **Quiet where it should be**:
- subagent sessions are silent, so one delegated

parent task does not ring for every child turn;
- a 500 ms grace period after `idle` cancels the ale

rt when queued input or an automatic continuation immediately starts again;
- one failure sound per
orks with current DSH**: settings render as a card in the 0.2.x **Plugins** page, with an automatic

fallback to the 0.1.x settings section.
- **No build step**: plain ESM host code plus a hand-written
`window.__ModuleLoader__` client bundle.
## Install
### Desktop app (`desktop` profile)
Install it as a **managed third-party plugin** from inside DSH — do not copy files into the profile
it as a **managed third-party plugin** from inside DSH — do not copy files into the profile by hand:

1. Open DSH → left sidebar → **Plugins**.
2. Click **Add plugin**.
3. Paste the repository address:
`https://github.com/hifengzy/dsh-sound-notify` (or the release tarball URL, or the npm package name

`dsh-sound-notify`).
4. Install, then restart DSH if it asks.
The package then appears under **Plugins → Installed plugins** with its own uninstall and update con
trols. The three sound switches are on its package page: **Plugins → Installed plugins → dsh-sound-n
he three sound switches are on its package page: **Plugins → Installed plugins → dsh-sound-notify**.
> **Why not copy files?** The Plugins page records a managed install in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/
package.json` (`dependencies` plus `dsh.profile.bundles`). Files copied into `node_modules` by hand
are invisible to the manager — no installed-plugin row, no uninstall button — and the next DSH deskt
op update prunes them because they are not a declared dependency.
Upgrading from the v0.1.0 manual install?
v0.1.0 copied the package into the profile by hand. Run the migration helper, then install through t

The helper removes the unmanaged copy and mount row while keeping your saved switch values, then pri
nts the managed install steps (paste the repository address into **Add plugin**).
### CLI-managed profiles (`web`, `headless`, custom profiles)
Pick whichever source you prefer — all of them are the same plugin:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the profile's app after installing. `dsh plugin add` installs the package into the profile a
nd appends `dsh-sound-notify` to `dsh.profile.bundles`; the package's own `cordis.patch.yml` mounts
-sound-notify` to `dsh.profile.bundles`; the package's own `cordis.patch.yml` mounts the plugin row.
For a custom profile, replace `web` with its name. Check that the plugin composed correctly:

## Settings
**DSH 0.2.x**: **Plugins → Installed plugins → dsh-sound-notify** (the package page, beside its inst
all/enable controls). The values live in the plugin entry's `config` in the profile patch (`$DSH_HOM
E/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`) and are read live on every notification.
**DSH 0.1.x**: **Settings → Sound notifications** (registered `sound-notify` settings namespace in `
$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`).
| Switch | Default | When off |

| Task completed | on | `success: false` — no completion sound |
| Task failed | on | `failure: fals

e` — no failure/API-error sound |
| Waiting for you | on | `waiting: false` — no approval/question/a

ure/API-error sound |
| Waiting for you | on | `waiting: false` — no approval/question/abort sound |
## Debugging
The desktop host has no terminal. Set `DSH_SOUND_NOTIFY_LOG` **before launching DSH** to get a line
for every decision and playback attempt:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Playback failures (missing file, no audio player) are logged too instead of failing silently.
## Platform support
| Platform | Player | Status |

| macOS | `afplay` | verified |
| Linux | `paplay` (PulseAudio/PipeWire) | requires `paplay` |
| Win
dows | — | no AAC CLI player; logs a diagnostic and stays silent |
## Compatibility
| DSH | Settings surface | Install |
| 0.2.x (current, incl. desktop 0.2.1-rc.3) | Installed-plugin package page over volatile `Config` |

app **Add plugin** / `dsh plugin add` / GitHub / tarball |
| 0.1.x | dedicated settings section ove
r a registered namespace | `dsh plugin add` / GitHub |
The host half only observes the event bus (`session/event`, `agent/status`, `user-questions/request`
) and never edits the session log or influences approval decisions (the question waterfall listener
always calls `next()`).
